In [[number theory]], the '''first Hardy–Littlewood conjecture'''{{sfn|Aletheia-Zomlefer|Fukshansky|Garcia|2020}} states the asymptotic formula for the number of [[prime k-tuple|prime ''k''-tuples]] less than a given magnitude by generalizing the [[prime number theorem]]. It was first proposed by [[G. H. Hardy]] and [[John Edensor Littlewood|J. E. Littlewood]] in 1923.<ref name="original">{{cite journal |last1=Hardy |first1=G. H. |author-link1=G. H. Hardy |last2=Littlewood |first2=J. E. |author-link2=John Edensor Littlewood |title=Some Problems of 'Partitio Numerorum.' III. On the Expression of a Number as a Sum of Primes. |journal=[[Acta Mathematica|Acta Math.]] |issue=44 |pages=1–70 |year=1923 |volume=44|doi=10.1007/BF02403921|doi-access=free }}.</ref>

==Statement==
Let <math>m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_k </math> be positive even integers such that the numbers of the sequence <math>P = (p, p + m_1, p + m_2, \ldots , p + m_k)</math> do not form a complete residue class with respect to any prime and let <math>\pi_{P}(n)</math> denote the number of primes <math>p</math> less than <math>n</math> so that <math>p + m_1, p + m_2, \ldots , p + m_k</math> are all prime. Then{{sfn|Aletheia-Zomlefer|Fukshansky|Garcia|2020}}{{sfn|Tóth|2019}}
:<math>\pi_P(n)\sim C_P\int_2^n \frac{dt}{\log^{k+1}t},</math>
where
:<math>C_P=2^k \prod_{q \text{ prime,} \atop q \ge 3}\frac{1-\frac{w(q; m_1, m_2, \ldots , m_k)}q}{\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{k+1}}</math>
is a product over odd primes and <math>w(q; m_1, m_2, \ldots , m_k)</math> denotes the number of distinct residues of <math>0, m_1, m_2, \ldots , m_k</math> modulo <math>q</math>.

The case <math>k=1</math> and <math>m_1=2</math> is related to the [[twin prime|twin prime conjecture]]. Specifically if <math>\pi_2(n)</math> denotes the number of twin primes less than ''n'' then
:<math>\pi_2(n)\sim C_2 \int_2^n \frac{dt}{\log^2 t},</math>

where
:<math>C_2 = 2\prod_{\textstyle{q \text{ prime,}\atop q \ge 3}} \left(1 - \frac{1}{(q-1)^2} \right) \approx  1.320323632\ldots</math>

is the twin prime constant.{{sfn|Tóth|2019}}

== Skewes' number ==
{{main article|Prime k-tuple#Skewes numbers}}
The [[Skewes' number]]s for prime ''k''-tuples are an extension of the definition of Skewes' number to prime ''k''-tuples based on the first Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.  The first prime ''p'' that violates the Hardy–Littlewood inequality for the ''k''-tuple ''P'', i.e., such that
:<math> \pi_P(p)>C_P \operatorname {li}_P(p), </math>
(if such a prime exists) is the Skewes number for ''P''.{{sfn|Tóth|2019}}

== Consequences ==
The conjecture has been shown to be inconsistent with the [[second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture|''second'' Hardy–Littlewood conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal | first=Ian | last=Richards | title=On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes | journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. | volume=80 | pages=419–438 | year=1974 | doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1974-13434-8 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Generalizations ==
The [[Bateman–Horn conjecture]] generalizes the first Hardy–Littlewood conjecture to [[polynomials]] of degree higher than 1.{{sfn|Aletheia-Zomlefer|Fukshansky|Garcia|2020}}
